title: Proportional memory reservoirs for weights, KV, and activations with activity-aware headroom
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Background: We routinely observe tail OOMs and conservative static reservations for KV and activation memory that reduce GPU utilization. Current heuristics statically reserve fixed margins per-tenant which either waste headroom or lead to fragile bursts when many requests hit large KV footprints. Goal: design and implement a proportional memory reservoir system that partitions GPU memory into three logical reservoirs (weights, KV, activations) with an activity-aware headroom layer that can be borrowed/returned safely during bursts. The system should reduce end-to-end token-cost by improving GPU utilization while maintaining SLOs and eliminating OOMs in >99.9% of steady-state traffic.
design_summary: 1) Baseline weight reservation: immutable per-device based on pinned model weights + quantization profile. 2) KV reservoir: tiered reservoir computed from observed steady-state percentile of resident KV size per-model and per-tenant plus a dynamic buffer proportional to short-term activity (requests/minute). 3) Activation reservoir: elastic allocation governed by batch-size classes and continuous-batching window, with soft limits and eviction hinting if pressure required. 4) Headroom reservoir: a shared soft pool implemented as tokenized borrowable credits with backpressure signals to the router when headroom falls below thresholds. 5) Admission & preemption: cheap requests (short sequences) get preferential admission; large activation allocations can be preempted to reclaim headroom using graceful eviction policy that saves minimal KV prefixes when possible. 6) Simulator and safety checks: offline simulator to validate headroom policies against historical traces and an online safety circuit that triggers fallback to smaller model variants or shed to dedicated throughput tier.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Complexity: adds allocation accounting and new runtime APIs which increases code surface. - Latency risk: aggressive reclaim can add eviction-and-prefetch churn impacting tail latency; mitigated by prefetch hints and gradual reclaim windows. - Memory fragmentation: tokenized reservoirs may fragment GPU memory across slabs; mitigated by bin packing and periodic compaction while idle. - Fairness between tenants: need policy rules to avoid noisy-neighbor starvation; enforce per-tenant min-reservations and credit decay rules.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): build accounting surface and per-GPU reservoir metadata; implement baseline weight reservation and KV percentile estimator with rolling windows; unit tests and offline simulator integration. Phase 2 (3 sprints): implement elastic activation allocator, borrow/return token mechanics, and router backpressure hooks; end-to-end benchmarks on dev cluster. Phase 3 (1 sprint): safety circuits and canary rollout with traffic shadowing; monitoring dashboards and runbook. Phase 4: incremental rollout to production with gradual traffic ramp and post-rollout analysis.
acceptance_criteria: - Reduction of wasted reserved memory by >=20% on aggregate across dev clusters in the 95th percentile of runs. - OOM rate for inference serving reduced to <0.05% across canary tenants. - No more than 5% regression in P99 latency for standard small-sequence workloads during canary. - Automatic fallback to compatible model variant occurs successfully when headroom threshold breached in 100% of simulated breach events. - Telemetry: per-GPU charts show borrow/return events and credit utilization; alerting fires at reserve depletion and unexpected preemption rates.
telemetry_and_alerting: New metrics: gpu.memory.reservoir.weights_reserved_bytes, gpu.memory.reservoir.kv_reserved_bytes, gpu.memory.reservoir.activations_reserved_bytes, gpu.memory.reservoir.headroom_credits, gpu.memory.reservoir.borrow_events, gpu.memory.reservoir.preemptions, tenant.memory.borrow_rate. Alerts: headroom_depleted (>=3 consecutive borrow events in 1m), preemption_spike (>5 preemptions/min), simulator_regression_detected (discrepancy >10% between simulated and observed borrow rates). Dashboards: per-cluster reservoir utilization, tenant-level borrow heatmap, long-running eviction traces.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests on CI. 2) Verify simulator against 30 days of historical traces (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/MEM/Reservoir+Simulator). 3) Deploy to staging cluster with synthetic burst scenarios, run stressbench (GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127). 4) Canary to 5% of production traffic limited to non-enterprise tenants, observe 72h. 5) Expand to 25% then 100% if metrics meet acceptance. 6) Postmortem and follow-up items added to this ticket.
runbook_snippets: - If headroom_depleted alert fires: 1) Check gpu.memory.reservoir.headroom_credits per-GPU. 2) If credits exhausted, escalate to preemption queue and trigger router to enable fallback models (route flag: routing.enable_headroom_fallback). 3) If repeated within 24h, run simulator to replay trace and open follow-up with priority P0. - If preemption_spike: review eviction traces and run compaction during low traffic window.
security_considerations: KV residence policies should not change tenant isolation guarantees. Shared headroom credits require audit logs on borrow/return events (integrate with existing audit pipeline). Security review required for any change that exposes per-tenant memory metrics externally.
